two-photon absorption processes in BR and their application to optical data storage.
the photochemistry of BR in the wavelength range between 500 and 550 nm, where no photochemical activity has been reported before.
the photochemical properties of BR in aqueous suspensions and in films.

the photo-induced anistropy in BR is a very sensitive indicator of the photochemistry of BR.
a photochemical conversion from BR to F(620), which can be considered as a stable intermediate, is induced in BR films using 532 nm laser light pulses of high intensity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the F(620)/P(360) transition is a new, stable and reversible photochemical transition that is induced by two-photon absorption in BR films and suspensions.
the F(620)-state is a stable and red-shifted photoproduct, that can be formed by means of two-photon absorption of high intensity laser light.
